**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (name, school, parents, family background etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **g)** Write a composition to illustrate the saying: *Time waits for no one.*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Explain the saying in the introduction.
2. A short story of a student, Ebot, who wasted time.
3. What happened at the end of the year.
4. A contrasting example of someone who used time well.
5. Conclusion with the lesson.

**Model composition (463 words)**

The saying "Time waits for no one" means that time keeps moving whether we use it well or not. A day that has passed can never be recovered, and people who waste their time will always regret it. This lesson was taught to me by the story of Ebot, a boy in my class.

Ebot was a clever boy, and at the beginning of the school year, he was among the first three students in our class. However, he was a great lover of leisure. Whenever the teacher advised him to study, he answered with a smile, "We still have plenty of time. The examination is far away." Instead of revising his notes, he spent hours in the video club, watching films and playing games, and he often went to bed very late. In the morning, he arrived late at school, sleepy and unprepared.

Months passed quickly. His friends, who studied every evening and used the weekends to revise, made progress, but Ebot remained where he was. When the teachers gave him assignments, he postponed them to the next day, and the next day he postponed them again. Soon he had a huge pile of unfinished work, and his marks started to drop.

Then the examination month came without warning. While the other students sat calmly in the hall and wrote their answers, Ebot sat with trembling hands. Many questions were on topics that he had never revised, and the time was too short for him to think. He left the hall in tears, knowing that he had done badly. When the results were published, he failed in four subjects and had to repeat the class. He cried and said, "If I could only have those months again!" But the months were gone forever.

In contrast, I think of my neighbour Mrs Ayuk, who sells vegetables in the market. She wakes up at four o'clock every morning, prepares her goods, and reaches the market before others. In the evening, she keeps accounts and plans for the next day. With the money she earned by using her time wisely, she sent her three children to university, and today she owns a small shop. When people ask her the secret of her success, she answers, "I never allow a day to pass without doing something useful."

These two examples show clearly that time is a priceless gift. We cannot stop it, buy it back or slow it down. The wise person plans each day, does today's work today, and rests at the right moment.

In conclusion, time waits for no one. If we use it well, it brings success, and if we waste it, it brings sorrow. Let us therefore treasure every hour while it is with us, because tomorrow may never wait for us.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | The saying clearly illustrated by one or two developed examples (story or life situations), in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion that states the lesson |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Explaining the proverb in general terms only, without a story or example to illustrate it.
2. A story that does not match the saying, or that never states the lesson.
